blocks.content: A RoleBinding is what actually grants a permission, connecting a Role (what is allowed) to a subject (who gets it), within one specific namespace.

This is the piece that finally makes a Role, covered in its own topic, mean anything, a RoleBinding names both a Role (or a ClusterRole, per the nuance covered in the previous topic) and a subject, and the binding between them is the actual grant.

blocks.alt: The connection that finally turns a Role definition into a real, active grant

blocks.content:
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: read-pods-binding
  namespace: default
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: my-app-sa
    namespace: default
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: pod-reader
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io

blocks.content: A RoleBinding itself lives within, and applies only within, one specific namespace, the actual grant only takes effect there, regardless of whether the Role it references is namespace-scoped or a broader ClusterRole.

blocks.alt: The grant itself is always confined to one namespace, this object's own scope

blocks.content: 3. Subjects Can Be Users, Groups, or Service Accounts
blocks.text: 3. Subjects Can Be Users, Groups, or Service Accounts

blocks.content: Exactly as covered in the RBAC and Service Accounts topics, a RoleBinding's subject can be a human user, a group of users, or a ServiceAccount, the exact same mechanism grants access to a person or an automated, in-cluster process.

blocks.alt: The same subject types covered throughout this module, granted access here

blocks.content: It is worth restating clearly: a Role by itself, as covered in its own topic, grants nothing, the RoleBinding is the object that actually turns a defined permission set into a real, effective grant for a specific subject.

blocks.alt: This is the object that actually does the granting, not the Role definition alone

blocks.content: Binding the my-app-sa ServiceAccount, covered in its own topic, to the pod-reader Role, covered in the Roles topic, grants exactly that Pod's identity read-only visibility into Pods, and nothing else, within that one namespace.

blocks.alt: A precise, real-world grant, tying together several concepts from this module

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: A RoleBinding connects a Role (what) to a subject (who), within one namespace, this is the object that actually grants a permission, not the Role by itself.
Its subject can be a human user, group, or ServiceAccount, the exact same mechanism grants access to a person or an automated, in-cluster identity alike.
